text:
[LSCO.3.10.1] Firing
order is the spec-defined total order of [LDET.5.1] and the only
author control over it is where a rule is written. If a decision
needs tighter latency guarantees than "fires in a spec-defined
order on the same engine cycle" — sub-millisecond response,
kernel preemption, hard real-time scheduling, life-safety
assurance — it belongs in a PLC, an RTOS, or a kernel-level
control path, not in DS. The rule-engine execution model has
latency floors that come from Rete matching, working-memory
maintenance, and observable cycle boundaries; those floors are
fine for home-automation and operational policy but inappropriate
for emergency-facing control.
